models_evaluated: U-Net-based brain metastasis detection and segmentation AI algorithm

links.outcome: AI sensitivity, false positives, and Dice on external datasets versus consensus reference standard
links.effect: FDA testing sensitivity 90.0%, DSC 0.86; augmented external cohort sensitivity 81.4%, DSC 0.70; open-access cohort sensitivity 85.2%, DSC 0.78, showing lower performance externally.
links.quote: In the augmented and open-access external validation cohort, a sensitivity of 81.4% (95% CI: 73.7%-89.1%) and 85.2% (95% CI: 83.0%-87.4%) with an average number of 0.22 and 1.19 FP lesions and DSCs of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.66-0.73) and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.77-0.78) were calculated, respectively.

links.outcome: AI performance across multiple datasets and institutions
links.effect: Performance varied across three datasets: sensitivity 90.0% (FDA multi-institutional), 81.4% (augmented), 85.2% (open-access UCSF-BMSR); DSC 0.86, 0.70, 0.78.
links.quote: This AI algorithm demonstrated promising performance via three unique datasets.

links.outcome: Physician qualitative rating of AI contours needing revision
links.effect: In the augmented external validation cohort, 46.3% of contours were rated as requiring major revisions.
links.quote: In the augmented external validation cohort, 46.3% of contours were rated as requiring major revisions.

links.outcome: Rate of AI contours requiring major physician revision
links.effect: 46.3% of contours in augmented external validation required major revisions, so authors conclude the tool needs physician oversight rather than autonomous use.
links.quote: However, given the notable rate of contour revisions, these findings support its clinical role not as an autonomous system, but as a human-in-the-loop tool requiring physician oversight.

screen.reason: The study conducts multi-institutional external validation and qualitative physician assessment of an FDA-cleared AI segmentation model, finding that high revision rates necessitate human-in-the-loop oversight, but it does not compare outcomes of a specific deployment practice.
